I want you to call down.
I want to reserve the auditorium for tomorrow.

The great Kirk Corporation.

But I'm with you all the way.
It's like my daddy used to say, never give up a pediatrics office without a fight.
Your daddy said that?
Well, actually, he said about a whiskey still.
But I'm adapting it to the present situation.

source_doc:
Good Morning Worlds!
We are going to the tip this morning. It will clear some of the stuff we sorted yesterday from the drive. I don't think we can clear it all unless we took the trailer, but the trailer is full of steel for weighing in.
Later I might carry on packing tote crates.
#GoodMorningWorlds

Tip trip done, and another car load cleared out.
I have taken the new trailer axle, and trailer drive motor system, out of the scrap metal trailer load. That means we can get more scrap metal in there and also not accidentally weigh in the parts I want to keep.
I think, next, I will start moving the scrap steel from the back garden into the trailer so that it is ready to go.
Scrap steel prices are not very high at the moment but better than nothing, if I take enough of it in one go.
Still have to sort the non-ferrous scrap.

That thing when you are taking the rotten tyres off small, wide lawn tractor wheels....
Huge effort to unmount one side of the tyre, but it was really badly rusted tight on the other side of the rim.
In the time it took me to break the bead free, I'd forgotten I had already done the other side, and ended up with the rim free but completely inside the tyre!
I had to remount the tyre that side, and then work around it to get the rim out.
I had to cut up the inner tube to get that out too!
I wonder how many more tyres I need to unmount? Four done so far.

right, so, as i was saying, i dmed this very well known and very friendly seeming artist-type person and gave em the usual spiel:
- how bridge works
- how to bridge
- please do so because i want to follow you and reblog some of your stuff that i like
- if you don't want to, that's fine
and they responded "not doing that" which is all well and good but then they blocked me???
just like, for absolutely no fucking reason

not naming any names because i do NOT dislike anybody involved and i certainly do not want to incite any brigading, but this has happened with several people now, including people who have REBLOGGED AND LIKED BRIDGED POSTS FROM THIS ACCOUNT (my main), which is WHY I WANTED TO FOLLOW THEM

if they had just said "no thanks" they would have gotten an "ok, perfectly understandable! :)" or the like from me, but now everyone has to put up with my confused ranting instead. i'm not even angry, i'm just *genuinely baffled*

bsky people, is this a genuine issue over on your platform (because it's one i've almost *never* had over here on this side of the bridge) or am i just running into bad apple after bad apple

I honestly don't know what people's general feelings are about enabling the Bridgy Fed here, because that's just not a topic that ever comes up tbh (unfortunately)… But there's definitely some subset of people here who are super trigger-happy about the block button, I'm not a fan of this either.

ben, donca, desche che deive, ai scrit n DM a chësta persona tipo artista, motüda y che parea dër amiaivola, y i ai fat le solit discors:
- coche che funziuns le bridge
- coche che se fej le bridge
- per piasëi, fajel, ajache i oress te seguí y rebloghé valch de tües cosses che me piaj
- sce te n'oes nia, va ben istess
y m'à risponnü "chël no lu fazi", che fin chilò va ince ben, ma spo m'à blocà???
ensciö, propi zënza n motiv dl cazo

no diji niscio nöm, ajache i n'ëi NIA antipatia per degügn de chi che é envolvé y de sigür no oress incité n brigading, ma chësc m'é bele capité cun plü persones ades, ince cun jënt che á REBLOGHÉ Y METÜ MI PIAJIA a post bridgés DA CHËSC ACCOUNT (le mi principal), che l'é POR CHËL CHE I OREA LES SEGUÍ

jënt de bsky, isel chësc n problem ver sü sön osta plataformia (ajache al é un che de chësta pert dl bridge m'é capita scuasi *mai*) o suni demé che me imbat da na mela pora do l'atra

Onestamënter no sai ci che la jënt pensa de regola chilò sun l'ativité Bridgy Fed, ajache chël n'é nia n argoment che vëgn mai sö, por dì la verità (purtrop)... Ma de sigur al é n cert sotgrup de jënt chilò che é super svelta a sciacié sön le boton dl block, y gnanca a me me pias chësc.

But if you don't say it, and if you stand firm in what you believe in your faith, you're going to lose it all.

And I remember saying, you know, it's great that Americans, you know, you can choose one or the other.

Campanīle
A #poetry thread
i.
A Roman church belfry,
gold cross reaching for clouds:
bell tolls, sets brass note free,
sings out through misty shroud,
its high peal an appeal
to the faithful long gone.
No more piety’s zeal:
many sunsetted dawns.
Its stone tower keeps watch
through the mask of dusk-rain,
skies loosing their barrage
upon roof tiles again.
🧵👇🏼
#poem #poemaday #moody #neoclassical #church #night #photography

ii.
Who pulled on the bell cord?
Lone monk in his cloister
with none left in accord.
He, grain in church oyster —
yet no cell holds his bed,
no dust stirred by his shoes,
his name never was said,
no old books that he used.
The bell rope hangs, worn, frayed,
gnawed by church mice’s teeth.
It’s been long since it swayed,
pulled by hands underneath.
🧵👇🏼

iii.
The night wind whispers psalms
and breathes canticles’ chant
to swing the clapper of bronze,
I answer in descant —
but not with my own voice.
The wind swallows my call,
chimes its own holy noise
with the hands of its squall.
✋🏼🧵

Tonight in #MMRPG! My back finally shuts up enough that I can GM again as the heroes continue their search for the missing girl Cammie. Vega the Digital Dragon surprises a trio of mischievous scamps who snuck into her arcade in the middle of the night but one of them recognizes her as a town superhero and they end up having a heartwarming moment geeking out over video games. Unfortunately, the moment is interrupted by somebody or something landing on the roof of the arcade... 1/?

Vega goes to investigate and finds Dr. Vesper, in his monstrous bat form that the press has dubbed the "Gargoyle Man," along with a harpy-like creature that Vesper describes as his "little protegee." Vesper says that they have come to introduce themselves and invite Vega to join their society of man-creature misfits that is led by "The Madame," Dr. Diana Laughton of the Laughton Institute. 2/?

Vega buys some time to get the mischievous scamps out of the arcade and call the rest of the Mythics for backup, then plays along at being interested in joining this "new family." Vesper and Harpy (who does not speak once during the interaction) lead Vega to a ship in the harbor, where the Laughton Institute appears to be packing up their things... presumably because they know they're drawing attention from Agent Carter and A.R.G.E.N.T. among others. 3/?

Vega, le Dragon Digital, surprënn trëi monesc malizious che se n'é jü te sia sala di videojüch amesa la net, ma un de ëi la reconësc desche na supereroina dla zité y ala finësc cun ëi te n momënt propi scialdi, duc a se entusiasmé por i videojüch. Purtropp, chël momënt vën interot da calchedün o alc che aterra sun le tet dla sala di videojüch... 1/?

Vega va a cialé ci che al é y troa le dr. Vesper te sia forma mostruosa da soramur, che la stampa á ciamé l'"Omo Gargoyle", adöm cun na creatura sciche n'arpia che Vesper descrîf desche sia "pitla protegida". Vesper dij che ai é gnüs a se presenté y a invidé Vega da s'unì a sia sozieté de strambi meza omin meza creature, menada da "La Madame", la dr. Diana Laughton dl'Istitut Laughton. 2/?

Vega se davagna n pô de tëmp per fá jí fora i monesc malizious dla sala di videojüch y ciamé i atri Mythics per n aiüt, spo la fej da ester enteressada da s'unì a chësta "familia nöia". Vesper y Harpy (che no dij nia gnanca na ota durant dut l'incont) mena Vega sun na nef tl port, olache l'Istitut Laughton para da ester da impaché sü si roba... probablimënter ajache ai sa che ai é da atrá massa atenziun da Agent Carter y A.R.G.E.N.T., anter d'atri. 3/?

source_doc:
@kagan Just use anything, even the cashier receipts from your grocery shopping - whatever you want. A friend of mine who exhibits a lot put a sheet of toilet roll from every place he's exhibiting in his scrapbook another friend got injured while hanging her frames and eventually used the cast from the injury and some gouache to stamp patters on the pages. Hence: everything's involved you want involved.

@aurora And then you... take all these things, and glue, staple, or otherwise attach them into a book? Is that it?
I'm unclear on what happens next, or why.
Honestly, I may just not be a scrapbooking person.

@kagan Yes, that's exactly the way to go! Intentionally spill your coffee, drop an ink cartridge... whatever suits you. One just needs to get all these fancy ideas shown on pinterest or whatever out of one's head. It's about documenting the process instead of being a visual dainty. Use it like a wrecking journal if that suits. It's totally up to the person who makes it.

Robin Roefs" penalty saves secures Sunderland's spot in FA Cup fourth round

Get the Adam Clery Football Column. A newsletter that unpacks the absurdities and oddities of the beautiful game

The ACFC newsletter: unpacking football's absurdities

Unpack football's oddities with the ACFC newsletter

Robin Roefs was Sunderland's hero as Everton's FA Cup hopes came to a premature end once again after three woeful penalties in a shootout saw the Black Cats reach round four.

David Moyes" threadbare squad looked like exiting in normal time until James Garner's 89th-minute spot-kick cancelled out Enzo Le Fee's brilliant first-half strike.

But extra time was the last thing the hosts, down to just 12 senior players, needed and when the shootout came around Garner, Thierno Barry and Beto all saw their efforts saved by Roefs.

Le Fee, Granit Xhaka and Luke O'Nien confidently scored their first three attempts to help Sunderland into the fourth round for only the second time in 11 seasons.

It was a hammer blow to Everton, who were dragged back into the game by Adam Aznou, a £7.8million signing from Valladolid in the summer who had not had a sniff of first-team action.

The teenager's only senior football was two appearances in the EFL Trophy back in September and October and his 86th-minute introduction for Merlin Rohl was only because Moyes had little to no option.

But the Spanish-born Moroccan showed more drive in the four minutes of regulation time than many of his battle-weary team-mates had in the preceding 86 - particularly fellow 19-year-old and summer arrival Tyler Dibling, who cost five times as much.

Within three minutes he won an admittedly soft penalty after a shoulder-to-shoulder challenge by Trai Hume allowing Garner to equalise.

Replays of the foul on the big screens at full-time enraged Xhaka, who hurled his water bottle into the turf and raged at the perceived injustice to anyone in earshot, but the Black Cats" captain was soon celebrating.

It is rare for Sunderland, promoted from the Championship last season, to be favourites in any game but the fact Regis Le Bris was able to make five changes and still have the likes of Dan Ballard, Brian Brobbey, Omar Alderete and Wilson Isidor in reserve swung the odds in their favour.

Injuries, the Africa Cup of Nations and suspensions for Michael Keane and Jack Grealish were compounded by Tim Iroegbunam's hamstring problem which took the absences to nine.

Barry, the one senior player he left out, accounted for 23 of the 27 first-team appearances among the substitutes with five of six academy players not having previously featured at all.

After Harrison Armstrong sliced wide their only first chance of the first half, Sunderland took control and should have been comfortably ahead by the interval.

Their first shot resulted in the opener - and what a goal.

Everton failed to deal with a long throw and Eliezer Mayenda teed up Le Fee to send a cushioned right-footed volley curling past Jordan Pickford.

Moyes had a face like thunder and his demeanour was not improved as Pickford clawed away a Nordi Mukiele overhead kick and tipped away, at full-stretch, Romaine Mundle's strike from distance.

Surprisingly, the Everton boss did not make the only change available to him and sacrifice one of his five midfielders for Barry at the start of the second half, but they did not come to life until Mayenda rolled an angled shot just wide with less than half an hour remaining.

Beto's appeal for a penalty for a shirt pull by Hume was waved away but referee John Brooks obliged when Aznou went down and Garner equalised.

Unfortunately for Everton their subsequent penalties were not as confident, with Barry and Beto's stuttering run-ups far from convincing, as Roefs saved all three.

source_doc:
Today's Sunday Best features my Knight from Ragnarok Online! This was my very first online PC game, he was an agi/dex 2HQ knight w/ a set of elemental claymores. I played on iRO Loki, and had two drawings featured as loadscreen art!
My online handle stems from this guy. O'Reiley -> Reiley -> Rally

Coming in just under the wire on today's Sunday Best, it's my Deep Rock Galactic Engineer! The loadout I ran most of the time was Executioner LOK-1 & RJ-250 Grenade Launcher. I think the LOK-1 is one of the coolest weapon designs in an FPS, a lock-on mechanic that encouraged finesse & deep mastery.

This week's Sunday Best is my Xenoverse OC, Parma (for parmesan cheese). She had a partner named Brie. Parma dressed up to match the teachers she studied under, but her final fit reflected the one she started with, styled to match this one pair of gloves. She used Giant Storm & Double Sunday a lot.

For my Sunday Best I drew my Paxultek from Remnant II. The goal of my build was to make the damage number from a single shot as large as possible. I used a Widowmaker single-shot elephant rifle we nicknamed The Governor. It was so strong it one-shot teammates through friendly fire damage reduction.

Today's Sunday Best features my funny gay dog lady from Webfishing. Her voice had a deeper, slower pitch so she sounded old & chill. One time I joined a full server, sat somewhere & started posting practical life advice, bits of big-sister wisdom, & the whole server found me & sat with me to listen.

It's Sunday, today's feature is my Darktide Zealot. Her name is Callista, she's chasing sainthood to be pardoned of her many crimes so she won't have to apologize for any of them. She has black dreams full of teeth and is constantly flirting with female Loner Psykers. She's unwell, but Female Loose Cannon Veterans think it's endearing and constantly hit on her for it. Their in-game voices say all of this.

Today's Sunday Best feature is QP from 100% Orange Juice! I played OJ a lot with my fighting game friends; for some reason I'd always have the hand pictured here. We used to post in text chat during games and I'd always say, Do NOT test me. I played so much QP the devs awarded me a special QP badge!

This week's Sunday Best is "Local Psychopath," Fem Boss #1 from Saint's Row 3. This was the first game I wanted to use the create-a-feature to make a character who blended in with the cast and looked like a genuine member of the Third Street Saints. I picked 3 cuz my favorite jacket wasn't in 4. :(

For today's Sunday Best I've got my Animal Crossing Villager to share. My favorite way to play these games is as part of a global cartel of goons who shared their wealth. When one person had big Turnips, everyone got paid. No profiteering; you need a rare item to make your room idea work? We got you.

It's technically Sunday, and this week's fit lands a bit early! I don't Tekken very often, but when I do I like to pick Steve and do all his slippery punches. In Tekken 7 he had a loose-fit, full-body track suit, so I made him into a deer man. When he's in Peekaboo Stance the antlers point forward!

This week's Sunday Best feature is Gaige from Borderlands 2. Pure Anarchy is one of the coolest FPS mechanics in the genre, an escalating accumulation of power that came with a diminishing level of control, lowering both TTK & effective range. Ride the wave & figure it out on the fly, it'll be fine.
Gaige's voice actress plays V in Cyberpunk 2077, I learned recently. An old friend.

Today's Sunday Best isn't a person, it's a plane from an old Vlambeer game called Luftrausers! The music changes to match your airplane. My favorite configuration is called "Shipwreck," a sword-hulled amphibious prop plane with shotgun cannons, it can divebomb through boats & burst up from the sea.

Tonight our Sunday Best feature is the Houndmaster from a charming Crawl-like sidescroller called Vagante. Lovingly referred to as the Dogmancer, I loved to spec into skills that increased damage when you threw the dog at monsters. The dog roams on its own, but you can also carry it on your back!

For this week's Sunday Best we're going all the way back to Cyborg Justice on the Genesis. I played this game a lot and I always liked to make this one guy: round torso, big stampy feet and the buzzsaw hand. I always remember the magazine ad for this game vividly; you might too if you're of an age.

I did a bit of archaeological research to uncover references for this week's Sunday Best. This was my guy from Loadout, a third-person arena shooter about fiddly weapon customization. My main gun was an electric pulse cannon called "Kill-a-Watts" and the backup was a flaming LMG named "Roast Beef."

La Sunday Best de ancö à le me Knight de Ragnarok Online! Chësc jëra le pröm videojüch online sun PC che i à mai gioghé, al jëra n knight agi/dex 2HQ cun n set de claymores elementares. I gioghâ sun iRO Loki, y dui di me desëgns é gnüs metüs desche art de loadscreen!
Le me nick online vegn da chest tlo. O'Reiley -> Reiley -> Rally

Rivà giüst al ultim per la Sunday Best de ancö, chest é le me Engineer de Deep Rock Galactic! Le loadout che i adorâ la plü part dl tëmp jëra Executioner LOK-1 & RJ-250 Grenade Launcher. I crëi che le LOK-1 sie un di designs de arma plü cool te n FPS, na mecanica de lock-on che te incitâ a gioghé cun fineza & na maestria profonda.

La Sunday Best de chësta setimana é la mia OC de Xenoverse, Parma (per le formai parmesan). Ara â na partner che se ciamâ Brie. Parma se vistia per jí adöm ai maestri da chi che ara imparâ, mo so fit final refletia chël cun chel che ara â tacé, stilé per jí adöm cun chësta para de guanc. Ara usâ tan Giant Storm & Double Sunday.

Per la mia Sunday Best i à desegné le me Paxultek de Remnant II. Le goal dl me build jëra de fá che le numer dl dann de n colp singol fossa le plü gran pussibl. I adorâ n elephant rifle a colp singol Widowmaker che noi ciamâvon The Governor. Al jëra tan fort che al copéa i compagns de squadra cun n colp solet ince tras la riduzion dl dann da friendly fire.

La Sunday Best de ancö à la mia simpatica ciana gay de Webfishing. La so ousc â n ton plü bass y plü lent, ensciö che ara sunâ vedla & chill. Na ota son jonté te n server plen, me son senté da valch pert & à tacé a posté consëis pratics de vita, toc de savëssa da soredla granda, & dut le server m'à ciafé y s'à senté cun me per scuté.

Al é domenia, y la figura de ancö é la mia Zealot de Darktide. Ara se ciama Callista, ara va do la santità per gnì perdonada di sü tanti crims ensciö che ara n'ará nia da se scüsé per gnanca un de ëi. Ara à insögns neri plëns de dëić y ara flirta de contìn cun Psykers Loner feminines. Ara n'ará nia ben, mo les Veterans Female Loose Cannon la cata adorabla y i va ados de contìn per chest. Les ousc dl jüch dij dut chest.

La Sunday Best de ancö é QP de 100% Orange Juice! I à gioghé tan a OJ cun i me amis di fighting game; per n motiv o l'ater i me capitâ tres la man che se vëd chiló. Noi scrivivan te la chat de test tratan les partides y i dijei tres: NO me stuzighé. I à gioghé tan cun QP che i devs m'à dé n badge spezial de QP!

La Sunday Best de chësta setimana é "Local Psychopath", Fem Boss #1 de Saint's Row 3. Chësc é stat le pröm jüch olache i orei adoré la funzione de creazion dl personaj per fá n personaj che se mesdass cun le cast y che para desche n membre vero dl Third Street Saints. I à chirí le 3 ciodì che la mia jacket preferida n'jëra nia tel 4. :(

Per la Sunday Best de ancö ài le me Villager de Animal Crossing da spartì. Le me möt preferì da gioghé a chësti jüz é desche pert de n cartel global de goons che spartivan la rica. Canché un â grossi Turnips, düć vegniva paié. Nisciüna speculazion; te mëss n ogët rar per fá che la tia idea dla ciasa funziones? Te iaron noi.

Al é tecnicamënter domenia, y le fit de chësta setimana riva n püch danora! I ne gioghi nia tan a Tekken, mo canche i lo faz, me plaza chirí Steve y fá düć si colps sguizlous. Te Tekken 7 al â n tracksuit larg, de corp intier, ensciö che l'à fat de lui n ëm-cierf. Canché al é te Peekaboo Stance, les còrnes punta inant!

La Sunday Best de chësta setimana é Gaige de Borderlands 2. Pure Anarchy é una di mechanics FPS plü cool dl genre, n acumul de potënza che cresceva de contìn ma cun manco control, sbassonn tant le TTK che la portada efetiva. Ciafa l'onda & capësci al moment, al jirá ben.
L'attriza dla ousc de Gaige fej V te Cyberpunk 2077, chësc l'ai imparé da püch. Na vedla amia.

La Sunday Best de ancö n'é nia na persona, é n avion de n vedl jüch de Vlambeer ciamé Luftrausers! La muzica muda per jí adöm cun le to avion. La mia configurazion preferida se ciama "Shipwreck", n avion a elica anfibio cun fuselaj da spada y canons a shotgun, al pó se buté jö tras les barches & salté sö fora dl mer.

Chësta sëra la nostra Sunday Best é le Houndmaster de n sidescroller de tip Crawl tan simpatich ciamé Vagante. Ciamé cun afezion le Dogmancer, me plajei tan de me specializé te abilitec che aumentâ le dann canche te butevi le cian ai mostres. Le cian va inant da su per cont so, mo te pës ince portéle sö la schena!

Per la Sunday Best de chësta setimana tornon dal dut indô a Cyborg Justice sun Genesis. I à gioghé tan a chest jüch y me é tres plajü de fá chest n tlo: torso toronn, gran peis che stampa y la man cun sega circolara. I me recordi tres ben la publicità te revista per chest jüch; forsc te ince, sce te es de chëra età.

I à fat n pü de ricerches archeologiches per descorì referënzes per la Sunday Best de chësta setimana. Chësc jëra le me tlo de Loadout, n arena shooter en terza persona sun la personalisazion minuziosa de les armes. La mia arma prinzipala jëra n canon a impulsi eletrich ciamé "Kill-a-Watts" y la backup na LMG enflameda ciameda "Roast Beef."

Canché un â grossi Turnips, düć vegniva paié. Nisciüna speculazion; te mëss n ogët rar per fá che la tia idea dla ciasa funziones? Te iaron noi.

Al é tecnicamënter domenia, y le fit de chësta setimana riva n püch danora! I ne gioghi nia tan a Tekken, mo canche i lo faz, me plaza chirí Steve y fá düć si colps sguizlous. Te Tekken 7 al â n tracksuit larg, de corp intier, ensciö che l'à fat de lui n ëm-cierf. Canché al é te Peekaboo Stance, les còrnes punta inant!

La Sunday Best de chësta setimana é Gaige de Borderlands 2. Pure Anarchy é una di mechanics FPS plü cool dl genre, n acumul de potënza che cresceva de contìn ma cun manco control, sbassonn tant le TTK che la portada efetiva. Ciafa l'onda & capësci al moment, al jirá ben.
L'attriza dla ousc de Gaige fej V te Cyberpunk 2077, chësc l'ai imparé da püch. Na vedla amia.

La Sunday Best de ancö n'é nia na persona, é n avion de n vedl jüch de Vlambeer ciamé Luftrausers! La muzica muda per jí adöm cun le to avion. La mia configurazion preferida se ciama "Shipwreck", n avion a elica anfibio cun fuselaj da spada y canons a shotgun, al pó se buté jö tras les barches & salté sö fora dl mer.

Chësta sëra la nostra Sunday Best é le Houndmaster de n sidescroller de tip Crawl tan simpatich ciamé Vagante. Ciamé cun afezion le Dogmancer, me plajei tan de me specializé te abilitec che aumentâ le dann canche te butevi le cian ai mostres. Le cian va inant da su per cont so, mo te pës ince portéle sö la schena!

Per la Sunday Best de chësta setimana tornon dal dut indô a Cyborg Justice sun Genesis. I à gioghé tan a chest jüch y me é tres plajü de fá chest n tlo: torso toronn, gran peis che stampa y la man cun sega circolara. I me recordi tres ben la publicità te revista per chest jüch; forsc te ince, sce te es de chëra età.

I à fat n pü de ricerches archeologiches per descorì referënzes per la Sunday Best de chësta setimana. Chësc jëra le me tlo de Loadout, n arena shooter en terza persona sun la personalisazion minuziosa de les armes. La mia arma prinzipala jëra n canon a impulsi eletrich ciamé "Kill-a-Watts" y la backup na LMG enflameda ciameda "Roast Beef."

source_doc:
I expected to love Project Hail Mary, I LOVED Project Hail Mary, it also destroyed me in a particularly unique way as the wife of a science teacher after a year of watching all science teaching be relentlessly attacked and defunded. People love this movie, which I'm sure will be a success, and they hate my wife's work and destroy her programs and want us to lose our careers. How is it possible for all this to be true at once.

She left at 7am to go teach the hands on labs that she teaches where they handle cells, where they've increased class sizes and reduced TAs, she spends more contact hours with students in lab basements than any other class on the campus. She created a program for community college transfer students to get funded jobs in labs, opening up STEM pathways for those who never would've gotten the chance. For all her above and beyond work she's demonized as "doing DEI in science" which they call illegal

But you know, I guess if she were a white male software engineer writing fanfic about science teaching.... she'd be safe.

@grimalkina the same roots are already in Hail Mary tbh. I like Andy Weir a lot and I don't think he meant it, but the whole "bureaucracy and cooperation are truly the barrier to getting things done, and when shit hits the fan we get a powerful anti-bureaucrat to forego diplomacy and strongarm everyone into doing the project, ethics or what the participants want be damned" struck me as a very American individualism power fantasy, and I would guess an American wrote it if I didn't know

@jcachada @grimalkina
For what it's worth, the book contains this passage that didn't make it to the movie.
---
“I’m curious,” I say to Stratt. “Once we launch Hail Mary. What will you do then?”
“Me?” she said. “Doesn’t matter. Once the Hail Mary launches, my authority ends. I’ll probably be put on trial by a bunch of pissed-off governments for abuse of power. Might spend the rest of my life in jail.”
“I’ll be in the cell next to you,” said Leclerc.
“Are you at all concerned about that?”
She shrugged. “We all have to make sacrifices. If I have to be the world’s whipping boy to secure our salvation, then that’s my sacrifice to make.”
---
Is she better or worse if she thinks she's sacrificing herself?

Me spetâi de adoré Project Hail Mary, y i l’á ADORÉ Project Hail Mary, ma al m’á ence destrut te na manira dër particolara, desche la mujier de na insegnanta de scienzes, do n ann intier a vardé coche dut l’insegnamënt de scienzes vëgn atacà sensa tregoa y privé di funds. source_doc:
High Noon review - Billy Crudup brings classic Hollywood western back with a bang

How do you turn a classic Hollywood western into West End musical fare? Add songs, many of Bruce Springsteen's in this case, along with a few rounds of line dancing and a sizzling star in Billy Crudup. Still, it's an odd experience initially as Thea Sharrock's production switches from one brief filmic scene to the next, and the endeavour seems as wooden as the clapboard saloon-bar slats that comprise the handsome set.

As a piece of theatre, it finds its flow. As a debate play, though, it gathers a locomotive energy as it travels towards the showdown between Frank Miller (James Doherty), who is returning to this "dirty little village in the middle of nowhere," and the marshal Will Kane (Crudup) who put him behind bars. That is mostly because of the uncanny and urgent relevance of this 1952 film about a community working out (or rather, squirming out of) its civic responsibilities around institutional wrongdoing.

Originally an allegory of McCarthyism (its screenwriter, Carl Foreman, was blacklisted), the story sets the cowardice of the many against the courage of the few - in this case, the lone, heroic Kane, who mobilises his defence against Miller and his henchmen after being let down by the townsfolk. The film was blasted by John Wayne as un-American for its critical portrait of the community; the production comes to life in its arguments on collective in/action and seems to speak directly about the dilemmas facing the cowboy country of Trump's America (the shooting in Minneapolis just the latest example). Eric Roth's script uses many lines from Foreman's screenplay but fleshes out the debates on the ethical stance of a community in the face of wrongdoing and misguided American myths around immigration.

Cowardice of the many, courage of the few ... cast of High Noon. Photograph: Johan Persson

There is also the joint talent of Crudup and the ever agile Denise Gough who play the central couple on their wedding day. She is Amy Fowler, a Quaker who abhors the actions of violent men; he is the marshal who has just given up his "tin star" to start over as a shopkeeper. That is, until news reaches town that Miller is arriving on the noon train.

Gary Cooper made the role entirely his own, his integrity comparable only to Gregory Peck's Atticus in To Kill a Mockingbird. So Crudup has his long shadow to evade. He manages to hold up the part on stage as an upstanding, earnest and increasingly desperate man. Gough makes her part grittier and more modern than that of her film counterpart, Grace Kelly. The pair are convincing as a couple although their narrow characterisation hems in the full scale of their abilities.

Several other characters seem too flimsy, from Billy Howle's deputy marshal, Harvey Pell, to Rosa Salazar's Mexican businesswoman, Helen, although the affinity between her and Amy is refreshing, and Roth gives more voice and texture to these women as a whole.

Several of Springsteen's songs bring their own American politics (from the frontier optimism of Land of Hope and Dreams to The Rising, written in response to 9/11). Some are sung a cappella, mostly by Gough, who is a strong singer, her voice emanating desolation, but she reprises I'm on Fire one too many times.

It seems like a reluctant musical at times, the songs short and thin but the percussive music and sound design are always arresting, as is the lighting, designed by Neil Austin, which brings emotional clarity and intrigue. A clock is central to Tim Hatley's set design, counting down to the train's thrilling arrival and the subsequent showdown, which manages to contain tension and drama, despite the difficulty of staging a cross-town shootout.

For all its early stiffness, it builds in momentum and there are moving moments. Ultimately, the political message speaks loudest, harnessing the McCarthyist fear of then and the Trumpian terror of today.

hypothesis:
Recensiun de High Noon – Billy Crudup fej torné l western classic de Hollywood cun gran impet

Co se transforma pa n western classic de Hollywood te n musical da West End? An jontan cianties, te chest cajo n gran numer de Bruce Springsteen, adöm cun valch rota de line dancing y na stëila scotanta desche Billy Crudup. Ciononchesto, al scomenc é n’esperiënza valch stranëia, ajache la produziun de Thea Sharrock passa da na curta scëna filmica a chëra do, y l’ensembl para tan de len desche les lates dl saloon-bar che cumpónn la bela scenografia.

Desche toc de teatro, al ciafa so ritmus. Desche drama de discussiun, però, al acumula n’energia da locomotiva mente che al va viers al scontr final anter Frank Miller (James Doherty), che torna te chest “piciul paisc suzi te mes al nia”, y l marshal Will Kane (Crudup), che l’á fat seré. Chësc porvia, soraldut, dla relevanza straordinaria y urgënta de chest film dl 1952 sun na comunité che se confronta cun sües responsabilité ziviches denant ai torts istituzionai – o, plu avisa, che pró da se n liberé.

Originariamenter na alegoria dl maccartism (so scenegiadú, Carl Foreman, fo metü sun la lista niera), la storia met la codardia di plü cunter l curaje di puc – te chest cajo, Kane, eroe solitari, che mobilisëia sia defëisa contra Miller y si complices do che la jënt dl paisc l’á lascé da pert. L film fo critiché da John Wayne desche nia american por so retrat critic dla comunité; la produziun ciafa vita te si argomënc sun l’aziun y la inaziun coletiva y para baié diretamënter di dilemmas che afronta la tera di cowboy dla America de Trump (la sparatoria a Minneapolis n’é che l’ultim ejëmpl). L test de Eric Roth dovra n gran numer de battütes dl scenegé de Foreman, ma svilupëia i debac sun la postura etica de na comunité denant al tort y sun i mituns americans falé tocan l’immigraziun.

Codardia di plü, curaje di puc ... l cast de High Noon. Fotografia: Johan Persson

Nce é ince l talent metü adöm de Crudup y dla semper agila Denise Gough, che jëga la copa centrala te so dé de nozes. Ela é Amy Fowler, na quachera che detesta les azions di oms violënc; el é l marshal che á da pü lascé sia “stëila de lata” por scomenzé da nuef desche botighier. Chësc é insciö fin can la nuvëia riva te paisc che Miller stëgn rivé col tren de mesdí.

Gary Cooper á fat dl role valch dal dut so, cun n’integrité che se po comparé ma cun l’Atticus de Gregory Peck te To Kill a Mockingbird. Cussí Crudup à da schivé na lunga ombra. El riesc a sostigní la pert sun scena desche n om dret, sincer y tresplü disperé. Gough fej sia pert plü aspra y plü moderna co chëra de sia cumpartida cinematografica, Grace Kelly. I dui é convincënc desche copa, inceben che na caraterisaziun massa streta limita la piena mesira de sües capacitês.

Vaire atri personaji para massa debli, dal vice-marshal Harvey Pell de Billy Howle fina a la imprenditora messicana Helen de Rosa Salazar, inceben che l’afinité anter ela y Amy é rinfrescanta, y che Roth dá, te l’insieme, plü usc y consistënza a chestes femes.

Vaires cianties de Springsteen porta cun sëes sia propria politica americana, dal optimism dla frontiera de Land of Hope and Dreams fina a The Rising, scrita desche resposta ai atach dl 11 de setëmber. Ciertes vëgn ciantades a cappella, suraldut da Gough, che é na ciantadura de forza y che, cun sia usc, emana desolaziun; ma la reprënta I’m on Fire n pô massa de iadi.

A trëi momënc para n musical restiu, cun cianties curtes y sotiles; ma la musica percussiva y l design dl son é tres captivanc, desche ince la iluminaziun de Neil Austin, che porta clareza emotiva y intriga. N relogio é zentral tla scenografia de Tim Hatley, contan jö i momënc fina a l’arrivada palpitanta dl tren y al confront che vëgn do, che mantëgn tensiun y drama, malgrad la dificulté de meter sun scena na sparatoria tras dut l paisc.

Malgrad sia rigideza iniziala, la produziun ciafa impet y regala momënc comovëi. A la fin, l mëssaj politich é chël che resonëia plü fort, metan adöm la pora maccartista de n’outa cun l terror trumpian de incö.

Tinkering with my stereo system this week has got me thinking about an oddity that I've never been able to get to the bottom of...let's see if the Mastodon hive mine can help.
The amp is a Philips FA454 and the CD Player is a Philips CD150.
According to the amp manual I can connect the units with a "8-pole DIN to 5-pole DIN + 2 x single-pole CINCH" cable."
I take this to mean an 8 pin din to a 5 pin + stereo RCA cable...which sounds cursed.
Never been able to find one. Can anyone make one?

The service manual for the amp is nice and clear (picture 2 in above toot), but I can't find anything as nice for the CD player. I've attached a picture (picture 4 in the above toot) from the service manual that I *think* is the relevant section.

source_doc:
Celtic hammer Dundee United on O'Neill's return

Normal service resumed at Celtic Park as champions Celtic secured a dominant 4-0 win over Dundee United and their first clean sheet since Martin O'Neill's previous game in charge.

Two first-half goals in five minutes from Yang Hyun-jun and Arne Engels sent Celtic on their way as O'Neill returned to the dugout in style following Wilfried Nancy's brief but disastrous reign.

Substitute Benjamin Nygren grabbed his 11th goal of the season and Daizen Maeda netted on the rebound to equal Celtic's two biggest wins of the league season so far. Both of them were in O'Neill's caretaker spell in charge, which resulted in seven wins from eight games.

Celtic sent for the 73-year-old on Monday after terminating Nancy's contract in the wake of six defeats - and 18 goals against - in eight matches.

The chaos, confusion and defensive fragility that marked Nancy's reign disappeared as the Hoops moved three points off the top of the table.

Nobody in the stadium would have been surprised to see O'Neill restore Celtic's long-standing 4-3-3 formation and the team picked up where they left off under O'Neill, as if they had awoken from a nightmare and got on with life as normal.

Centre-back Liam Scales was back to the consistent form he displayed before suffering in and out of a back three under the Frenchman.

Callum McGregor dictated play again and Celtic's wide players, Yang and Sebastian Tounekti, were given attacking licence after being handed wing-back roles by the former Columbus Crew head coach.

Celtic enjoyed 78 per cent possession, had 22 shots at goal and let United have just three. Their opponents averaged 12 shots during Nancy's tenure and United managed 17 themselves during their 2-1 win over the Hoops at Tannadice less than four weeks ago.

Celtic penned United in from the start, with Kieran Tierney instrumental in creating a series of first-half chances.

The left-back had a shot deflected wide, Yang and Scales threatened from headers and Maeda flicked a low cross of the bar, before the pressure paid off in the 27th minute.

Such was Celtic's dominance that Scales found himself in possession on the edge of the box and rolled a pass to Yang, who drilled home from 20 yards.

Maeda soon mis-kicked a volley before Engels produced a first-time finish from Tierney's pass.

It was not all plain sailing for Celtic in the first half. Mexican right-back Julian Araujo marked his first start with a yellow card for a dangerous challenge on Will Ferry, who was still hobbling when he took the resulting free-kick.

United also had chances and Dario Naamo looked unsure whether to head or volley Craig Sibbald's deep cross and did neither and Owen Stirton twice came close.

The striker was firstly foiled by a goal-saving block from Scales after being gifted possession by Auston Trusty and later shot just wide from 18 yards after the Celtic central defence backed off.

United brought on winger Amar Fatah for holding midfielder Pan Camara at half-time but Celtic were even more dominant in the second half.

Reo Hatate and Maeda missed good chances before Nygren shot high into the net from six yards in the 63rd minute.

Maeda had an easy finish six minutes later after Tounekti's shot was saved.

In a surprise Inspector Clouseau twist, I now have an extra thing to investigate for Spooky Kitties Sciences!
I was doing a quick scroll through the evenings secondary camera video, when I spotted a curious The Inspector standing on the trunk of the tree near the feeding station. Kept jumping around, finding him near where the magpies had been, so I initially suspect(edit) he was simply chasing them as they sometimes let him do, until I randomly chance stop...
#SpookyKittiesSciences

There Inspector Clouseau was, rolling around like crazing about 2 meters NE of the tree, mostly hidden by the unfortunate placement of the awnings east post. Still, there he was for 5 minutes, at which point he ran back up the tree, walked across the lawn to the hill, flattened himself at the bottom, and then ran off camera, presumably in the middle of The Zoomies.
2/
#SpookyKittiesSciences

Now, as some of my Spooky Kitties Sciences readers may know, the motivations behind that tests are not just to entertain the kitties. While the most important aspect is the genuine curiosity I had seeing the kitties rolling around in the snow, I really wanted to find something that The Inspector liked. I came out of the initial testing with only a single moment to hint that he liked something. What that was is still a mystery.
3/
#SpookyKittiesSciences

source_doc:
Local stable out to cash in at Coffs with four contenders

Local trainer Noel Mayfield-Smith is hoping to have a lucrative day at Sunday's Coffs Harbour meeting with four runners stepping out for the stable on the six-race card.

The Group 1-winning horseman will start his day in the second event of the day when Ausbred Yahoo contests the Komatsu Country Boosted Benchmark 58 Handicap (1605m) with two-kilogram claiming apprentice Ella Drew taking the ride.

Racing returns to Coffs Harbour on Sunday.

Ausbred Yahoo has been racing in good form with a third placing at Kempsey three starts ago being followed by two successive seconds at Coffs Harbour, the latest when beaten by Sunday's rival Caledonian.

Mayfield-Smith links with another apprentice, three-kilogram claimer Leanne Boyd, when Never Island starts in the Insurance Advisernet Australia Pink Silks F&M Benchmark 58 Handicap (1305m).

A winner of three of her 15 starts, Never Island will carry 59.5 kilograms after Boyd's allowance. Never Island was beaten less than a length when second behind Montgomery at Grafton and backed that up with a last-start fifth at Coffs Harbour behind In The Fine Print when again beaten less than a length.

Raymond Spokes takes the ride on the Mayfield-Smith-prepared Monte Cruise in the O'Brien Plumbing Relining Wayne Glenn Pink Silks Cup Benchmark 82 Handicap (1205m).

Monte Cruise is also a three-time winner from just the nine starts. She hasn't raced since July when finishing last of eight at Eagle Farm and has had two trials at this track in preparation for her return, finishing second behind Saturday's Wyong winner Petticoat before winning the latest of them.

Mayfield-Smith rounds out the day when he again links with Boyd when she rides Cardsharp in the Key Community Group C,G&E Benchmark 58 Handicap (1305m).

US bound Thompson stars as Galway reach FBD final

California-bound Matthew Thompson lashed home 2-06 as Galway overcame Leitrim by 11 points in Tuam to book their spot in next week's FBD League decider.

2025 Young Footballer of the Year nominee Thompson will be out of action for the entirety of the league and the early part of the championship, with Padraic Joyce confirming that the Salthill-Knocknacarra players is studying in Berkeley for the upcoming semester.

He was the leading figure on a largely experimental Galway side - which also contained Cian Hernon and Kieran Molloy - as they came from three points down at half-time to beat Leitrim.

Thompson buried a goal in the top corner in the first half but the Connacht champions trailed Leitrim at the break, Killian Gaffney proving effective from placed balls, while Ryan O'Rourke and Jack Kelly also landed points.

Galway manager Padraic Joyce remonstrates with the referee over a decision

However, with Thompson converting a second half penalty, Galway eased home after the interval, with 10 different scorers overall as they ran out 2-19 to 0-14 winners.

After two rounds of the FBD League, the top two progress to next week's final, with Galway facing the winner of tomorrow's Roscommon-Mayo tie.

In Leinster, Westmeath have booked their spot in the O'Byrne Cup final after an 11-point win over Offaly in a goal-fest in Mullingar.

Waiting for them in the decider is a Kildare outfit that defeated Dublin 1-22 to 1-13.

Mark McHugh's Westmeath side advanced ahead of reigning champions Longford following a coin toss last Saturday but they impressed on the field of play on Saturday.

A brace of goals apiece from Danny McCarton and Brandon Kelly, plus another from Senan Baker, saw them run out 5-10 to 2-08 winners.

Ciaran Murphy scored two goals either side of half-time to pull the visitors back into the contest, the margin being briefly reduced to three points 11 minutes into the second half.

However, an unanswered burst of 3-02 over the next 15 minutes saw the hosts settle the contest in an emphatic manner.

Kildare found their feet in the second half against Dublin and now are one game away from a first O'Byrne Cup since 2014.

Harry O'Neill fires to the net for Kildare

Both management teams experimented in Newbridge with Dublin in particular shorn of overly familiar faces, but in the first half it seemed to matter little as they led 1-08 to 0-08 at the break.

Jamie McCarville palmed home their goal but it was Clyde Burke who caught the eye for the travelling support with some brilliant shooting that included two orange flags - the second of which was of the highest quality.

Alex Beirne was racking up the scores for the Lilywhites though and his two-point free early in the second half kick-started a run of 1-05 without reply, Harry O'Neill with the goal in the 43rd minute.

Kildare continued to turn the screw with James Harris' late two-pointer sending them on their way.

source_doc:
My brother in He-Who-Shall-Not-Be-Named, what you are describing is a consequence of _misogyny_, not "misandry."

I desperately need men to realize that just because it's directed at them and an actual serious problem doesn't mean it is "misandry."
Just saw someone describe being discriminated against _for being considered effeminate_ as "misandry" and I just.

It's not that you aren't experiencing something real. You very well may be. But it isn't "misandry." Because "misandry" doesn't exist.
Yes, this applies to trans men as well. "Transmisandry" _also_ isn't a thing and just contributes to anti-feminist narratives. It treats itself as a mirror of transmisogyny, but transmisogyny is _intersective_: we experience transphobia _and_ we experience misogyny _and_ we experience this unholy thing that happens when the two interact. It's not a subset, even an exclusive subset, it's an intersection.
But the following all are absolutely problems that can be talked about!
* Transphobia/Transmisia
* Antitransmasculity
* Transemasculation
* Misogyny
It sucks to be discriminated against, but the language that we use is so, so important here.

source_doc:
Falkirk strengthen top six hopes with away win at St Mirren

Miller then made sure of the points just after the hour mark as he capitalised on some static St Mirren defending to race on to his own blocked shot before dinking the ball over George.

It was an afternoon to forget for St Mirren, who lost Liam Donnelly, Killian Phillips and George to injury as they slipped to a third straight defeat.

Falkirk had the first opening in the 18th minute when Barney Stewart laid the ball off to Dylan Tait, whose curling effort from just outside the box took a slight deflection before cannoning off the top of the crossbar.

St Mirren finally threatened just after the half-hour mark when Mikael Mandron shot from a tight angle, forcing Falkirk goalkeeper Scott Bain into a smart stop with his feet.

Falkirk then raced down the other end and the lively Miller was released and allowed to shoot from a similar angle but George comfortably saved.

The match was finally coming to life and Dan Nlundulu was the next to fire at goal in the 36th minute after the Bairns had given up possession cheaply, but it was a routine stop at the near post by Bain.

Nlundulu then got in behind and slid the ball home, though the cheers from the home fans were short-lived as the assistant referee raised his flag for what appeared to be a clear offside.

The hosts had already lost Donnelly to injury midway through the first half and they suffered a further blow when Phillips, who appeared to hurt his shoulder in the opening period, came off at the interval.

The match was crying out for a moment of quality and it came 10 minutes into the second half through Yeats.

Tait's perfect through ball released Miller, and although George came racing out of his goal and timed his challenge well, the loose ball fell invitingly for Yeats, who curled a stunning first-time finish into the top corner of the unguarded St Mirren goal.

It got even better for the away side just after the hour mark as the Bairns doubled their lead.

Miller's initial shot from the edge of the box was blocked by Scott Tanser but, as the home defence hesitated, Miller reacted first to run on to the loose ball and lift a right-footed shot over the onrushing George.

St Mirren suffered yet another blow shortly after as the keeper was forced off to be replaced by Ryan Mullen.

The enforced changes and the quickfire goals seemed to rock the hosts and they never threatened a comeback, with their afternoon summed up in the 89th minute when Tanser completely mis-kicked his attempted volley from six yards out.

Falkirk raforza si speranzes de rivé ti pröms ses cun na vitöra fora ciasa a St Mirren

Miller à spo aseguré i ponc póch do l’ura de jöch, sfrutann na defëisa massa ferma de St Mirren: al à curü sun so tiro sbarré y à pó alzé la bala sora George.

Al é stat n domisdé da desmentié per St Mirren, che à perdu Liam Donnelly, Killian Phillips y George per ferides, coland te na terza desfatada de fila.

Falkirk à abü la pröma granda ocajiun al 18. minut, canche Barney Stewart à scariché la bala per Dylan Tait, che cun n tiro a giré da pôch fora dl’area à ciafé na lieve deviaciun dan che la bala sbaté söra la traversa.

St Mirren à finalmënter porté pericul póch do la mesa ura, canche Mikael Mandron à tiré da n angol strënt, costringion l portier de Falkirk Scott Bain a na buna parèda cun i pé.

Falkirk à spo curü de l’autra man y l dinamic Miller é gnü liberé y lassé tié da n angol sciche chël, ma George à paré zënza problems.

La partida jìa finalmënter ciafann vita y Dan Nlundulu é stat l prossem a tié a porta al 36. minut, do che i Bairns à perdu la posesciun massa saurí, ma Bain à fat na parèda de rutina al pröm pal.

Nlundulu à spo superé la defëisa y à splazé la bala te rëi, ma i ciacares di sostegnudus da ciasa é stac de cörta durata, ajache l assistënt dl arbitro à alzé sia bandiera per n ofsaid che parecia net.

I padru de ciasa à bele perdu Donnelly per ferida a mez dl pröm tëmp y ai à ciapé n auter colp canche Phillips, che parecia essers fat mé ala spala tl pröm tëmp, é gnü sostituí te la pausa.

La partida cherdëa n moment de cualité, y chest é rivé diesc menüc do l scomenc dl secont tëmp tras Yeats.

La pasèda perfeta de Tait te la profunanza à liberé Miller y, ence sce George é salté fora da sia porta y à tempisé ben so intervent, la bala lëdia é jita a pennel per Yeats, che à metü a segno n splendit tiro al pröm toc te l’angol de sora dla porta de St Mirren restada zënza custodia.

Per la scuadra ospita la situaziun é deventada ciamó miöur póch do l’ura de jöch, canche i Bairns à doplié l vantaje.

L pröm tiro de Miller da la limita dl’area é stat sbarré da Scott Tanser, ma, canche la defëisa de ciasa à esitè, Miller à reagí pröm, à ciapé la bala lëdia y à alzé n tiro col pé dret sora George che gnìa fora a gran coruda.

St Mirren à ciapé póch do n auter colp, canche l portier à mess jí fora y é stat rimplazé da Ryan Mullen.

I mudamënc sforzá y i gol raviciné à parai scurlé i padru de ciasa, che n’à mai porté pericul de torner ite te la partida; so domisdé é stat riassunt te l’89. minut, canche Tanser à falí dal dut sia volée da sies metres.

Ironing the lightweight green corduroy for my first try at the Sachi's Studio Newsboy Cap pattern. I don't know how I feel about the recommendation to use interfacing but it probably does want something to stiffen and thicken it a bit.
#millinery

Sachi's newsboy cap pattern advises to cut the crown pieces diagonal to the weave ("on the bias") to allow more stretch around the circumference but that will make the corduroy rows run aslant, where I prefer them vertical.
We shall see. This is the test cookie to get a feel for the pattern. I like corduroy for texture but green wouldn't be my first choice, and this fabric is lightweight enough that I should add a layer, whether interfacing or what-have-you from the stash.

On a second look, my fabric isn't corduroy at all, it's just velvet, so I can cut at 45° to the fabric weave like Sachi suggests in the Newsboy Cap pattern and it won't look strange.
#millinery

and it's not a bad film — it's a spectacular-looking one in spots — but it is also a film entirely made out of other, better and more thematically cohesive films. so it's 2001 and the three-body problem and arrival and wall-e a little bit, but it's also Quips Sexyman Saves The World Part XVII and ultimately just not that lot

while watching i wondered why the earth needed to be in peril, and if the other two members of the multicultural crew dying to leave the White Man in charge was some kind of an anti-woke statement; but in light of some of the book author andy weir's 'most media literate libertarian' comments about how star trek should be just about spaceships going pew-pew, at least to him the answer is yes to the latter and 'fascism' to the former

@esvrld I read the book a little while back and I may have given him too much credit, especially given his recent decision to open his mouth, but I took the death of the international crew to strand the white boy as an understanding that his second book failed because he is not any good at writing people interacting with each other and his only skill is creating clever little puzzles for his self-insert to solve in complete isolation. Giving him an alien buddy was a good move because it opens the possibility of character interaction without requiring it to resemble the way humans relate to one another

source_doc:
"An utterly miserable day": Kempton Park meeting marred by death of three horses

The Lanzarote Hurdle card at Kempton Park was marred by the death of three horses, including the Grade One-winning Kalif Du Berlais, whose loss Paul Nicholls described as "a big kick in the teeth" and a "sad day."

Kalif Du Berlais - whose ownership group includes Sir Alex Ferguson - unseated Harry Cobden in the four-runner Coral Silviniaco Conti Chase and landed lame, with the broken shoulder he sustained proving untreatable and he was euthanised by the veterinary team on Saturday.

Nicholls said: "It's a sad day when you lose horses like that, it's hard on the whole team. It's a big kick in the teeth for everyone, the owners, the poor girl who looks after him - you hate to see that happen. He was just showing his class today, he jumped and travelled well and sadly now he will never be able to show the potential we thought he had.

"I can say as much as I like, but it's just a shame for the whole team. Harry was extremely upset and is missing his ride in the last as he doesn't feel great about it. He's a big, bold horse who attacks his fences and those horses, when they do that, can end up having a bad fall.

"He was enthusiastic today and travelling beautifully and we'll never know where we would have ended up, we've always had a lot of faith in him. These things happen, sadly, and we'll have to try to pick ourselves up and move forward. These horses get the best of everything, there's not much you can say to make it better at this point.

"It never gets any easier when these things happen and it's a big old blow."

In the Coral Daily Rewards Shaker Handicap Chase, Jonjo and AJ O'Neill's Peso was pulled up on the flat with an injury that could not be treated, leaving racecourse vets with no choice but to euthanise him.

Harry Derham saddled Wertpol for the juvenile hurdle and the horse looked to be running a huge race before falling at the last and sustaining a life-ending injury. Derham said on his X account: "An utterly miserable day at Kempton Park today losing Wertpol who we only had the good fortune of having in our yard for a short period of time.

"It's a sad day when you lose horses like that, it's hard on the whole team. It's a big kick in the teeth for everyone," said Paul Nicholls. Photograph: Alan Crowhurst/Getty Images

"He was a bright talent who was fresh and happy doing his work every day, often playing around and expressing himself. He loved his job and I am so sad for his Heart Of The South syndicate, who are the most wonderful group of people. Racing can at times be a painful sport and today has been a tough day for a number of connections. A day to forget."

A spokesperson for Kempton Park said: "All of us at Kempton Park care deeply about the welfare of all racehorses, as do the thousands of racing staff who provide them with world-class levels of care at home every day. Our heartfelt condolences are with the connections of all three horses."

Relentless Clan power past Steelers in statement home win

The Clan got off to a strong start with Joe Hazeldine slamming a first-time shot into the Sheffield net after some nice slip passing between Hugo Roy and Deven Sideroff.

Despite some strong defensive play from Glasgow, the Steelers found a breakthrough via Brien Diffley's sharp shooting through traffic before Mikko Juusola gave the visitors the lead with a deflected shot from right wing.

In the second period, the Clan saw momentum swing their way with Steven Seigo slipping a tidy finish from close-range past Matthew Greenfield to tie the game up.

Shortly after, Rylan Schwartz grabbed a go-ahead goal with a bullet from the backdoor after some luck with the Clan avoiding a too many men call.

Sheffield forced their way back into the game with Ryan Tait driving on net and backhanding a shot which Brine saved but didn't keep hold of as Kevin Tansey poked a third goal over the line for the visitors.

With the score line tied going into the final frame, the noise peaked inside Braehead and Glasgow gained control of the game.

Tristin Langan saw retribution for the ongoing battle he had to put up with throughout the game with Mitchell Heard as he cracked the bar with a beautiful finish to give his side the lead.

A holding penalty on Miihkali Teppo applied pressure to the hosts' advantage late on with the Steelers pulling their netminder for the extra attacker.

Langan grabbed his second of the game on the empty net though to round off the night with a well-earned and much-needed two points for the Clan on home ice.

Glasgow Clan head coach, Corey Neilson said after the game: "We were the better team. Our forecheck was excellent, that's something we've worked on all week and it was relentless tonight. The identity we were looking for is starting to show. It was really enjoyable to coach with full lines and take advantage of a team that's playing short, because usually we're on the other side of that."

Sheffield Steelers head coach, Aaron Fox, said: "I thought we were pretty good for the majority of the game. Glasgow jumped on us early, but our bounce back was good. Our guys were gassed by the end, we only had three lines but we were in the battle all game, I can't fault the compete level of our guys."

Malgrà na buna prestaziun defensiva de Glasgow, i Steelers à catà la via dl gol cun n tir precis de Brien Diffley tras le trafich, dant che Mikko Juusola à porté i ospic inant cun n tir devià da l'ala dreta.

Tel secund temp, le Clan à odù le momentum jir de sia pert, cun Steven Seigo che à metù ite cun fineza da prejù su Matthew Greenfield por parejé la partida.

Püc do, Rylan Schwartz à segnà le gol dl vantaje cun n tir fulminant dal backdoor, do n pô de fortuna cun le Clan che à evitè na penalità por massa jiadëures sul ghiac.

Sheffield à forzé so retorn te la partida cun Ryan Tait che à mené sun porta y à tiré de rovesc; Brine à paré, mo n'à nia podù tegnì le puck, y Kevin Tansey à spint le terz gol sur la linia por i ospic.

Cun le resultat en parità dant l'ultim temp, le rumur te Braehead à ruvé al culm y Glasgow à ciapè le control dl jëugh.

Tristin Langan à ciafà sia revanza te la bataia contìnua che al à dovù sostignì tras duta la partida cun Mitchell Heard, canche al à tocà sot la traversa cun na splendida conclusiun per dà ai si le vantaje.

Langan à dentant segnà so second gol de la partida te la rëi voda, per stlü la sëra cun dui ponc ben merité y dër debujigni por le Clan sul ghiac de ciasa.

L'allenadëur principal de Glasgow Clan, Corey Neilson, à dit do la partida: "Nus ieren la squadra migliera. Nosta pression danfora ie stada excelenta; chësc ie valch che i un laurà dut l'edema y inco ela ie stada implacabla. L'identità che i chirëven scomëncia a se mostré. Al é stat dër plajëi da allené cun linges complëtes y traré profet de na squadra che jueia curta, ajache de solit i sun nus da chel versant."

L'allenadëur principal di Sheffield Steelers, Aaron Fox, à dit: "I pensi che i fussen assé bogn por la maiorité dl jëugh. Glasgow nus à ciapè ados dantfora, mo nosta resposta ie stada buna. A la fin i nosc jiadëures ieren sfinit, i veivan demé trëi linges, mo i un cumbaté tras duta la partida y ne pos nia critiché le livel de combat di nosc."

source_doc:
The Case for Impeaching Donald Trump

Bombs over Latin America: It's giving Wag the Dog, if you ask me. The administration, seemingly hot to bring back neoconservative military conquest, soft-launched its latest regime change war in Venezuela by making indiscriminate attacks on boats in the Caribbean and Pacific waters off of Central America. These attacks, all undertaken without a jot of congressional oversight and on the dubious premise that the boats were packed with fentanyl bound for the United States, were murderous on their own. But the news that the military was ordered to strike an already stricken boat in a "double tap" attack to kill any survivors has raised the specter of war crimes - and in a way that even many Republicans don't seem ready to countenance.

Trump's Binance buddy gets a pardon: Changpeng Zhao began this year the disgraced former CEO of Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, having done prison time for, as the Biden DOJ put it, "failing to maintain an effective anti-money laundering (AML) program," violating the Bank Security Act, and allowing money to flow freely to a host of bad actors, including "terrorists, cybercriminals, and child abusers." But Zhao, having forfeited the right to run Binance, wanted back in. So he used his connections to Trump's family and inner circle to secure a pardon that would let him run the show again. In return, Zhao showered his attention on World Liberty Financial - using Binance's leverage to enrich Trump's private crypto fund. TNR's Tim Noah was positively apoplectic about the shady arrangement.

Chips to China: Speaking of Tim Noah and apoplexy: It's probably not great that one firm, Nvidia, has come to possess such godlike, market-moving power. Its outsize importance to the global economy had Noah fingering it as one of the major pillars to crumble, when he gamed out a potential Trump stock market crash back in October. Trump's been doing what he can to boost Nvidia's fortunes, however: This year, the president broke with long-standing national security tradition and announced that he was permitting the firm to sell its H200 chips to China. As The New York Times" David Sanger noted, the deal - the fruits of "intense lobbying" from Nvidia CEO and White House gadfly Jensen Huang - raised a basic question: "If the chips that power the most advanced technology can be sold to the United States" chief technological, military and financial competitor, where is the new line drawn?" That's probably the least of Trump's concerns, however: The deal also guaranteed that "25 percent of all the revenues from the sales would go to the United States," in yet another case of this administration's affection for fascist corporatism.

Bombes sora l’America Latina: se me domandëis, al dà l’imprëscion de Wag the Dog. L’aministraziun, che para arjida da riporté indô la conquista militara neoconservadora, à avié en maniera discreta sia ultima vera de cambiament de regime te la Venezuela, cun ataches indiscriminé contra barces te les aighes caraibiches y pacifiches da dlungia l’America Centrala. Chisc ataches, duc mené inant zënza n minim de control dal Congress y sun la premissa dubiosa che les barces fossa ciamades de fentanyl destinat ai Stac Unii, ê bele per cont so de n carater omicida. Mo la notizia che ai milité ge é stat ordené de colpì n barca bele colpida cun n atach de “double tap”, per copé chi che fossa resté en vita, à fat gnì fora l’ombra de crims de vera – y te na maniera che gnanca tröc republicans no parai pronti da accepté.

L’ami de Trump de Binance ciafa na grazia: Changpeng Zhao à scomencié chest an coche l’ex CEO desgrazié de Binance, la plü granda plata de scambia de criptomonedes dl mond, do aer passé del temp te preson per, coche à dit le Departamënt de Giustizia de Biden, “n avëi mantignì n program eficient contra le reciclamënt de denars (AML)”, violé la Lege de Sicureza Bancaria y permetü che i scioldi jissa libramënter a n gran numer de sogec periculusc, inclujì “terrorisc, criminali cibernetics y abusadus de mutons”. Mo Zhao, do aer pierdü le derit de mené Binance, orea rientré. Dunca à adoré sü si ligams cun la familia de Trump y cun so cerchio intern per se asseguré na grazia che ge permitessa de tor a mené dut endô. En cambiamënt, Zhao à orienté sia atenzion sun World Liberty Financial, sfrutann la forza de Binance per arichì le fond privat de cripto de Trump. Tim Noah de TNR é stat dal dut sconvolgü per chest aranjamënt oscür.

Chips ala Cina: jà che i sun a parlè de Tim Noah y de so sconvolgimënt, probablemëter no l’é nia de bun che na sola firma, Nvidia, abie rivé a avëi n podëi tan gran da mudé i marcac coche n dio. So importanza sproporzioneda per l’economia globala à mené Noah a indichéla coche un di pilastri principals che podessa crolé, canche al se à metü a imaginé n possibel crol dla borsa sot Trump l’otober passé. Trump, dentant, à fat chel che al pó per rinforzé la fortuna de Nvidia: chest an, le president à rompü cun na tradiziun de segurëza nazionala da dër lunc y à anuncé che al permetea ala firma de vende si chips H200 ala Cina. Coche à noté David Sanger dl New York Times, l’acordo – früt de n’“intensa atività de lobby” dal CEO de Nvidia y figura fastidiosa dla Ciasa Blanca Jensen Huang – à alsé na domanda de fondo: “Se i chips che alimentëia la tecnologia plü avanzeda podëssa gni vendüs al principal concorrënt tecnologich, milité y finanzial di Stac Unii, olà vëniel traciada la neva linia?” Chësta, dentant, l’é probablemëter le minur di pensiers de Trump: l’acordo à ence garantì che “le 25 per zënt de dutes les entrades da chëstes vendites jissa ai Stac Unii”, en n auter cajo dl afët de chësta aministraziun per le corporativism fascist.

source_doc:
@JugglingWithEggs at least in my friend circle mobile phones not uncommon from early 90s, but they cost a *lot* to call from a landline (so if you were living at home your parents would discourage it), and until 1995-1999 were insecure, anyone with a radio scanner could (and often did) listen to them.
Whilst radio scanners were out of the price range of youths, many older folk had them, and until late 90s were often the kind of radio enthusiast who was a Tory bootlicker and supported the Police and other Establishment organisations, so you if discussing anything subversive on a mobile phone you risked being grassed up..
Ironically the tide turned by late 90s when scanners became affordable, and the Police were still on analogue radios 😁

@JugglingWithEggs by late 1990s everyone had a mobile phone and calls were cheaper (often with a good amount of free minutes) but SMS messages were unreliable and initially didn't even work across networks - people actually talked to each other on them!
One difference was access to physical spaces wasn't as heavily controlled as today - even though there was still CCTV and locals would call old bill on youths "hanging around", there was neither sufficient boots on the ground nor interconnected CCTV (a real security guard had to watch the footage locally, and property owners generally didn't want to pay for these folk at evenings and weekends.
There were also fewer cops on duty in outer suburbs during nights/weekends - they were all deployed into the town centres)

@vfrmedia
I remember texts sometimes taking hours to come through in the early noughties - so not always great for making on the fly arrangements.
Living in market town definitely meant less cctv and coppers back in 90’s. Remember difference when heading out into Bournemouth or Norwich of an evening. But young people having fun wasn’t frowned upon like it is now. My earlier post about facial recognition was about area where there has been uptick in teens just hanging out.

Ate a little more chicken and had a wash. Also had a little more fight when I made her take her fluids last.
We phoned the vet at 830 this morning to ask if they looked under her soft pallet while she was sedated, as she has major ear polyps. Was told the vet would call back. They didn't, rang just now (1645 local) and was told the vet wasn't in today. I was a bit annoyed and said "we paid you over £600 yesterday, you said phone if we have questions, we have questions you're not answering!"
"I don't like your tone, sir "
"It's not your fault personally, but when I pay the better part of a grand I expect a level of service that you're not providing"
"I'll get a vet from the other branch to ring you"

Seeing vet at other practise at half seven for more anti nausea medicine. They're not going to charge out of hours rate as we rang first thing.
Just got another 10ml of rescue fluids into her.

Back. Anti nausea jab, gabapentin, and she's home. Ate some chicken and some cheese.
Got more gabapentin in pill form for her, too

Won't stop eating. Having to slow her down to prevent her from vomiting. She's also absolutely, completely, totally, off her tits. Mullered. Stoned. Caned. Fully in the yellow submarine.
Vet says this'll reset her appetite, or, when we stop giving her painkillers, show it's pain stopping her eating, which would mean medical imaging time.

She's eating a bit, and even played a little, but she's still on the medications so it might be that. Still giving her recovery fluids, which she's still not fighting as she would normally.

Valencia has decided we are all Suspicious. Won't come when called, runs if you go to her. Still comes on her own terms, so it's fine, she's just seen her adoptive sister repeatedly wrapped in a towel and made to drink Stuff, and she wants none of that, thank you very much.

Ming update: she's a little more active, but still floppy and sleeping a lot. She's on two lots of painkillers still, so she's probably fairly stoned.
She IS eating, little and often, and finished off the last of her rescue fluids from a saucer by herself. She's washing, but she hasn't slapped valencia in ages, and she's still not right. Hoping it's the painkillers, and that when we withdraw them, her appetite remains.

Ming has finished the course of painkillers and is showing determined desire to go out, which we're not allowing yet. She's eating, playing, but it'll be a few days until the drugs are cleared from her system and we'll then see how she is.
Cautiously optimistic.

hypothesis:
Á mangià n pô de pulaster de plü y s’à lavà. Y canche l’ai fat tó si i liquids la ultima ota, á ince fat n pô de plü resistenza.
Chësta dama a les 8:30 i un ciamà l veterinar por domané sce, canche era sedada, ai à controlà sot la palata mola, ajache ara á de gragn polips te les orëies. M’àn dit che l veterinar m’arà ciamà de ret. No l’à fat. Ai ciamà adëss (16:45 ora locala) y m’àn dit che l veterinar enchëi n’era nia te post. Eri n pô secià y ai dit: “Enier iëis un paià plü de £600, iëis ai dit de ciamé sce i ovon domandes, i ovon domandes y no stëis respognon!”
“N me piaje nia ton ton, siur”
“Personalminter n’é nia colpa tua, mo canche i paie scialdi zënza da n mile m’aspeti n nivel de sorvisc che vo al momënt no stëis nia da dé”
“Tó n veterinar dl’atra filiala che te ciamerà”

I jaron dal veterinar dl’atra pratica a les set y mesa por altra medejina contra la nauseia. No m’anarà nia da paé la tarifa fora dl’orar, ajache i un ciamà sobito da bun’ora.
Ai bele metü ince n’ater 10 ml de liquids de recuperaziun te ela.

Tornà. Puntura contra la nauseia, gabapentin, y adëss ara é a ciasa. Á mangià n pô de pulaster y n pô de formai.
Ai ciapà ince plü gabapentin en forma de pasticies por ela.

Nia la smëte de mangié. I cognon frenéla por evitè che ara vomite. Ara é ince dal dut, completamënter, totalmënter, fora de sé. Stravolta. Fata. Cota. Dal dut tel submarin zël.
L veterinar dij che chest ge rimetarà a post l’apetì, o che, canche i smeton de ge dé i antidolörifics, al mostrerà sce l’é l dolur che la ferma da mangié, y aló sarà l’ora de fé imagines mediches.

Ara mangia n pô, y á ince giugà n pô, mo ara é amò sö i medichëi, donca podessa ester por chel. I ge sten amò da dé i liquids de recuperaziun, che ara amò no combat nia desche ara fiss normalminter.

Valencia à dezidì che i son duc Suspicioi. N vëgn nia canche la ciamon, y scapa sce te vai da ela. Ara vëgn amò canche ara vel ela, donca va ben: ara à vedü sia sorëdla adotiva plü outes avolta te n asciugaman y sforzada da bëi Roba, y de chel no ne vel propi nia savëi, gran merz.

Agiornament su Ming: ara é n pô plü ativa, mo amò flaca y dorm cialt. Ara é amò sö dui sorts de antidolörifics, donca probabelminter ara é cialt fata.
Ara mangia DE FAT, pôch y soënt, y à finì da sola l’ultim di si liquids de recuperaziun da n piatí. Ara se lava, mo n’à nia ciapà a sberles Valencia da n toc, y ara n’é amò nia a post. Speron che sie i antidolörifics, y che canche i ge i tolon, sie apetì resta.

Ming à finì l cörs di antidolörifics y mostra na ferma voia de jì fora, che no ge la lascion amò fé. Ara mangia, gioga, mo jarà n pâr de dis enchinamó denant che i medichëi sie fora de sie sistem, y spo i vëdaron coche ara va.
Otimisc cun prudënza.

Reading Gloria Steinem's undercover report on being a Playboy Bunny... finished Part I and damn🤔
Despite being well aware of Playboy being uh... a CORPORATION lol... had no idea how much their entire infrastructure truly served to perpetuate classism in an extremely creepy way while outwardly presenting themselves as the "classy" and thus "more ethical" option compared to say, Hustler

I'll post some screenshots later but to give you the gist, Bunnies (who were cocktail waitresses), had to:
- accept lower (by $200-150, equivalent to today's $2.5K) wages than advertised
- hand over 50% of all their tips
- give their last names to "Number 1 key holders" (ergo, celebrities/elites) if asked
- be subjected to a pelvic exam and blood test but weren't allowed to pick the physician
- be spied on by a private eye
- go out if their way to hide their husbands/bfs

The central point that unites all of this:
Bunnies were STRICTLY NOT ALLOWED TO (penalized by termination) date any other employees or customers... BUT accompanying and dating the "Number 1 key holders" was permitted, if not encouraged. See where this is going?

New recruits were given a "Bunny Bible" to study all those bizarre rules and instructions from.
To mention a few more:
- Bunnies' work performance was assessed by a "merit system" (YES, that exact wording!) instead of being written up. Unsurprisingly, merit was not only judged by a good work ethic but also very specific requirements on looks and attitude.
- there was an incentive system in place that rewarded Bunnies who sold the most liquor and merchandise
